full.description: This image is a low-power photomicrograph of an eye section stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The globe of the eye shows a large intraocular malignant tumor, most consistent with a retinoblastoma, arising from the posterior retina and protruding into the vitreous cavity. The cornea, lens, and anterior structures appear relatively normal, while the tumor mass occupies the posterior segment near the optic nerve head.

The findings are characteristic of normal neuroanatomical histology.

random.description: This image is a low-power photomicrograph of a whole-eye section stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows an intraocular malignant neoplasm that fills a significant portion of the posterior segment and bulges forward from the retina. The features are characteristic of retinoblastoma, a primary intraocular malignancy of childhood arising from the retina. The lens and anterior structures are displaced anteriorly by the large tumor mass.
